doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Anti-Festival and how the band got booked at Newport
summary: She recalls the Newport anti-festival, an afternoon slot, and guesses the Guild's press got them booked, with Kimery noting Wein's broad programming.

blocks.x: So that’s interesting, so I assume that the band itself, knowing George Wein and
the way he programmed them is probably something earlier in the day.
Ok. Did it seem like those bands that he, maybe, weren’t as popular or experimental or...
... didn’t want to program it earlier and left it up to the... So how, with... who convinced George that, or how did it go about that George agreed to have the band perform there, was it through?

Well I don’t know. I had played earlier at the Anti-Festival, you know there was maybe... there was another festival at Hilton at the same time and people who played like that kind of music were in it. It was in Newport in a tent, same town, same time, and we were having a festival to complain about the Newport festival.
So everybody that couldn’t play at it were allowed to play. So how did I ever get to play? It must be that maybe it was booked when the Guild existed...
... And the Guild had some kind of press going for it.
And then the Guild had broken up but these players were still the same.
And the word Guild was gone, so maybe it was that. You know I don’t really remember.
Well my sense with George Wein was that he wanted, within his programming he wanted to have the broadest breadth of jazz represented.
